reason: E1 directly states that annealing at 700 °C produces an FCC + B2 microstructure with ~900 MPa yield stress and >20% ductility, supporting the first three premises. However, the cited evidence does not address the proposed mechanism of reduced dislocation pile-ups, leaving the fourth premise unsupported.
premises: Annealing at 700 °C transforms the eutectoid nano-lamellar microstructure into an FCC + B2 microstructure in the Al0.3CoFeNi alloy.
The FCC + B2 microstructure is more damage-tolerant than the nano-lamellar (FCC+L12)/(BCC+B2) microstructure.
The FCC + B2 microstructure retains high tensile yield stress (~900 MPa) and achieves tensile ductility >20%.
The mechanism involves reduction of dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries due to a more stable microstructure.
